prize_parts.citation: For the development of general palladium-catalysed carbon-nitrogen cross-coupling

statement.case_for: I keep B057 as my single-part position, unchanged from round 1. Pd-catalysed C-N coupling is a general enabling method with four decades of independent confirmation and a mechanism that has been examined at the level of isolated and characterised intermediates (oxidative addition, amine binding and deprotonation, C-N reductive elimination). Ligand design by Buchwald and Hartwig, working independently, is what turned a narrow, tin-dependent reaction into a routine one across pharmaceuticals, agrochemicals and materials. It is the only candidate on the shortlist where maturity, attribution and mechanistic evidence are all settled at once. The chair's round-1 summary shows that the other three single-ballot positions each carry an open item that bears on the citation itself: the PROTAC versus glue credit cut and the absence of an approved degrader for B068, in-cell relevance for B022, and priority and the 2024 prize for B027. B057's open item is only novelty relative to 2010, which is a question about how we word the citation and not about the evidence.
statement.case_against: The strongest reservation is unchanged: the 2010 prize honoured Pd-catalysed cross-coupling, and a second prize in the family needs a stated reason. My answer is that C-N coupling was not a transfer of C-C chemistry to a new partner. Amines coordinate and poison the catalyst, beta-hydride elimination competes, and C-N reductive elimination from Pd(II) is intrinsically harder than C-C. Solving these required dedicated ligand classes and mechanistic work. Even so, a committee that reads the family as one idea will see a sequel. Kosugi and Migita precedent is also not carried by a two-name citation. Finally, if degraders are mature by the time we vote, B068 may represent the larger conceptual step, and I am not dismissing that.

responses.point: Chabes argues that PROTACs and cereblon glues share one mechanism, redirection of an E3 ligase, so a single citation covering Crews, Deshaies and Handa is honest, and that the clinical lag is a reason for careful wording only.
responses.response: The shared mechanism is real, but the chair's summary shows that Aili, Aqvist, Somfai, Sparr and I read PROTAC design and glue discovery as separate achievements, and your own file concedes that a single citation covering both is uncertain. As a structural chemist I would add that the evidence is uneven between the strands. The cereblon mechanism was established by Handa's target identification and by crystal structures that came after the drugs were already in use, whereas for PROTACs ternary-complex structures exist for only a minority of degraders. A citation worded around the mechanism has to be backed by structure for both, and I would want the committee to confirm that before treating one sentence as covering both. In my round-1 reply I also pointed to Shokat's KRAS work as your top-three alternative. That was a misreading of the shortlist, and I withdraw it. The comparison I should have made is between B068 and B057 on settled evidence.

responses.point: Aqvist treats degraders as a new pharmacological principle (induced proximity), holds a Crews, Deshaies, Ciulli configuration, and accepts that if maturity is weighted heavily, C-N coupling is the safer choice.
responses.response: We agree on the facts, and I accept that induced proximity is a new principle, which is why B068 is now my first alternative. We differ on the weighting. Your point that Ciulli's structure-guided VHL ligands and ternary-complex work are what made degraders rational is one I find persuasive from a structural standpoint. It also shows that the third name in B068 is a real choice between two strands (Ciulli or Handa), and you list Sakamoto's share in the 2001 proof of concept as unresolved. With the third seat contested and no approved degrader, I judge the case for B068 not yet equal in maturity and attribution to B057. If the experts' reports settle the credit and the clinical picture moves, I would reconsider.

responses.point: Somfai holds B057 with Buchwald and Hartwig, would acknowledge Kosugi and Migita in the background text or wording, and says the overlap with the 2010 prize is the strongest reservation.
responses.response: I agree on the configuration and on the novelty question. On Kosugi and Migita, I still prefer to carry the acknowledgement in the citation through the words general and catalytic, because the tin-amide reaction was narrow and used toxic reagents, and the general catalytic method is what Buchwald and Hartwig delivered. A background-text acknowledgement is a good complement but should not replace this. I do not agree that the novelty question is only about wording: the committee should say explicitly that amine binding, catalyst poisoning and C-N reductive elimination required their own ligand and mechanistic solutions. Without that statement the 2010 overlap objection from Aqvist, Aili and Sparr remains unanswered, and I would rather answer it than hope it fades.

responses.point: Linke, the chair, prefers B022 with Hyman, Brangwynne and Rosen and ranks B057 second as fully mature and unambiguous in impact, while asking whether Pappu and Mittag add quantitative work not covered by Rosen.
responses.response: Your ranking of B057 second is the cross-support I think the committee needs, and I read it as agreement on maturity and attribution. On B022 I cannot yet join you. The chair's summary records that six members doubt that functional claims are settled, and I share that doubt. In vitro phase behaviour is quantified well, but as a structural chemist I ask whether in-cell liquid demixing has been demonstrated independently of overexpression or crowding artefacts. A citation 'organises the interior of living cells' makes a claim about cells and not about test-tube demixing. If the committee wanted to proceed, I would hold the citation to the physical-chemical principle and name the founding observation, and Pappu and Mittag's sequence-encoded driving forces argue for treating the third seat as open.

responses.point: Sparr prefers B022 because the supporting measurements (valency, saturation concentration, material properties) are chemical, and wants physical chemistry and the chemistry of life fairly represented next to synthesis and methods.
responses.response: I accept that the measurements are chemical and that representation across the field matters; I would be comfortable with B022 as my first alternative if the in-cell question were settled. The risk I see is that the measurable quantities (saturation concentration, valency) are defined for reconstituted systems, and your own case_against notes that some droplets may be artefacts of overexpression or crowding, and that it is not always shown that a condensate does something a stoichiometric complex could not. That is a limit on the citation, not only a caveat. On representation, I would respond that B057 is also a chemistry of enabling methods that every other field uses, and the Nobel Prize in Chemistry has long honoured that. I do not think conservatism is a reason to prefer a field that is less settled.

responses.point: Brzezinski prefers B027 (Wolynes, Onuchic, Fersht), calls it complementary to the 2024 prize, and notes that credit is shared with Bryngelson and Dill.
responses.response: I see the logic of pairing theory with Fersht's phi-value experiments, and I agree the 2024 prize concerned prediction and design and not why folding works. My concern is the one you raise in your own file: the three-name limit leaves out Bryngelson and Dill, whose priority claims you call real, so the credit set is already uncertain. Sparr and the chair also question what the funnel predicted beyond what folding kinetics showed. On structure grounds, I would ask whether phi-value analysis really maps transition states at atomic resolution or infers them from mutational kinetics. Until those priority and predictive questions are answered, I do not see B027 reaching the clarity of B057.

uncertainties: Whether the committee accepts that C-N coupling is a distinct mechanistic achievement and not a sequel to the 2010 prize.
Whether a two-word signal (general, catalytic) is enough to acknowledge Kosugi and Migita, or the committee wants a fuller acknowledgement.
Whether degraders will be mature enough by the final ballot, in credit and in the evidence for both strands, to displace B057.
I remain less able to judge computational chemistry and chemical biology on their own terms; I rely on colleagues' written assessments for those fields.
statement.conflict_note: No specific conflict with B057 or my alternatives (B068, B024). My research is in electron crystallography and porous materials, which are not part of this configuration; I am a Stockholm University colleague of the Secretary, which is a colleague relationship and not a candidate connection. No recusal is needed.
